title: The bond linking inhabitants of the same area through space and time is inheritance

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The bond linking inhabitants of the same area through space and time is inheritance

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The deep affinity uniting the living and extinct inhabitants of the same area, independent of physical conditions, is due to inheritance from common ancestors, while the differences among regions arise mainly from modification through natural selection and only subordinately from the direct influence of physical conditions.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This bond, on my theory, is simply inheritance, that cause which alone, as far as we positively know, produces organisms quite like, or, as we see in the case of varieties nearly like each other.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XI, “Geographical Distribution”; section “Affinity of the productions of the same continent”. Scope: all organisms within a geographic area, living and fossil

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch11-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Regional phylogenetic continuity is testable with existing data. The asserted causal apportionment between natural selection and direct physical effects remains confounded and only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether regional living and fossil assemblages share phylogenetic ancestry beyond environmental matching, then partition trait and lineage turnover among inherited regional history, selection-associated environment, and direct plastic responses. Support requires strong geographic phylogenetic continuity not explained by physical conditions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Inheritance, selection, and direct environmental effects are not cleanly separable observationally.

Fossil and living taxonomies are unevenly linked.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.87
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Molecular relatedness of regional faunas and floras is testable with open trees and sequences, and that test is independent of the morphological pattern it is meant to explain. The further split between natural selection and the direct action of conditions does not fall out of those data. The resolvable part is common ancestry of regional biotas, not the mechanism of their differences.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Ask whether regional biotas form phylogenetic clusters on molecular trees built independently of the morphological resemblance naturalists scored, and whether regional trait differences exceed what the physical environment predicts. Shared ancestry can be assessed that way; attributing the differences mainly to natural selection remains weakly separated from other causes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selection, drift, and direct effects of the environment are not separated by present distributions.

A tree built from the same traits that display the affinity would make the inheritance test circular.

Joint phylogenetic and geographic coverage is partial for the full living and fossil scope.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.5
